## Appointments grid: seamless (2026-10-25)
Her ask (Google Calendar beside the LCM week): "i ike the spacing from google calendar, seamless. make mock of calendar in lcm." Mock `calendar-seamless-mock-2026-10-25.html` (artifact 9kqqqmTGMrNUHUo94fwMnJ); her 8 picks, all the recommended ones; "build it".
- **Look (CSS, Appointments calendar block ~4097-4210):** blocks edge to edge, 6px corners, no shadow, a 1px white seam (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #fff`); hour hairlines only (`#E6EDF0`, the half-hour gradient and the long-day `i.hh` rules are gone), no today wash; hover = `filter: brightness(1.05)`, no scale; blocks stack by `--z` (3 + column), hover 20, open card 19, search match 18.
- **Day head:** small MON over a big date (display font, 24px; 17px in a 28px circle at ≤900px), today's date in a teal circle, the visit count and the month are gone. The `${cake}` slot stays where it was (the one-calendar session renames it).
- **Nesting (`phApptCalDayBlocks` + `phApptCalBlockStyle`):** a cluster whose visits all start together (`it.same`) shares the width in halves; otherwise column 0 is full width and a later column sits over it from 45% across (each further one 15% more, 75% at most), `--z` keeps later ones on top.
- **Behind (`phApptCalGridHtml`):** a visit that meets one of her own grid events gets `it.under` and is drawn 10px in, so the event's colour shows at its left. `b.narrow` from `phC22DayLayout` is no longer read. Her events' own lane / dashed look is the one-calendar session's (`phC22LifeHtml`, `.ph-c22-*`), asked to go full width, solid tint, behind.
- **Fills the window:** `phApptCalEndFor` = the last booking's end rounded up to the half hour (4 hours at least; nothing booked keeps 7 AM - 9 PM); `phApptCalPxm` = the measured room / the span (34px an hour at least, 180 at most); the long-day map's busy stretches share the room the free bands leave. `phPinApptZones` reads the room off the body's own min-height (100dvh less the chrome: `innerHeight` disagreed with `dvh` by 20px in the pane) and redraws once (60ms debounce, latest room wins, at most 3 in 1.5s, never with a card open or while typing in the search; the first open keeps its rise-in). First open guesses `innerHeight - 190`. A phone keeps 66px an hour. The now line hides past the end (`phApptCalNowTick`).
- **Tested (Browser pane, localhost:8994, seeded bookings + her events through a stubbed `phC22Src`):** 1280x800 week: the grid ends at the last booking, body 614px = room 614px, no inner scroll; 9:30 / 10:30 / 11:00 nest (11:00 at 45%), two 2:00s in halves, a visit over Travel 10px in; teal circle on today. 375x760: 66px an hour, no sideways scroll, circles 28px. Prescriptions search narrows live and returns. No console errors from the grid.
- **Pages checked:** Appointments (week grid desktop + phone, day head), Prescriptions (search).
- **Not tested:** her real week with Cliniko colours; the Key2's 360 x 469; her own events drawn behind (waits on the one-calendar session's `phC22LifeHtml` change).
- **LIVE:** build 20261025-100100 (her "push live"; the stack fold 5ffbcb1d and the Me Routines list 71234172 rode along).

Her synth22 after the Me build went live: "as the only person that uses lcm, i want to be able to balance my life commitments and work commitment. i want the calendar to be a one space where i can see and manage work and life. need peoples birthdays to be visible. need to be able to take care of myself e.g. lunch breakfast fitness etc. i need a sleek design that holds alot of functions but is simple in design", with screenshots: "i need to see my whole page" (the grid cut at 3 PM; Lunch / Code slivers beside a patient; Breakfast / Gym chips on every day), "see birthdays and all day events", "i want to click and drag events", "i want my cycle day to show like birthdays". Guide `one-calendar-guide-2026-10-25.html`, mock `one-calendar-mock-2026-10-25.html` (MOCK = BUILD); her 13 picks; "build it". Built on the seamless grid (the other session's build the same day, which took pick 5: the hours fill the window).
- **Her picks:** 1 birthdays = cake + name + age chip in the row above the day · 2 cycle day in the DATE LINE ("CD 25"; a period day rose with the drop; the expected period a dashed rose pill) · 3 read from her OWN patient record's Cycle page, the record picked ONCE in the Me drawer · 4 routines = ONE ⟳ chip whose ring fills as they are ticked, tap unfolds · 5 clinic hours fill the window · 6 a routine that meets a patient = a faint full-width BAND behind the patients with its name in a pill at the right edge, never a lane; a one-off stays a block · 7 evenings = one ⟳ under the day · 8 her things drag: move (15-minute snap, a time tag) and stretch (bottom edge), a repeating one This day | Every day, toast + Undo · 9 a dragged PATIENT block drops into Edit prefilled, Save confirms · 10 cross-day drops in the week view · 11 tick = one tap on the pill, the second undoes, ✎ opens the card · 12 phone: same row, CD and drag (long-press lifts) · 13 "yes, mock it".

## 2026-10-26 · Lighter update check (what made LCM heavy)
- **Her ask:** "look at what makes LCM heavy" (the folder audit had noted the Key2 page weight).
- **Measured** (live build 20261025-211400): the page the phone gets is 7.77 MB, 1.76–1.81 MB compressed: code 1.46 MB (83%), styles 0.27 MB, icons almost nothing. What each area adds compressed: pictures 181 KB, Fang Bing Ren / Ren / Patterns / Guide 173, Care Plan & Treatment 150, tap and key handlers 140 (most of it the one 507 KB binding block in `renderPharmacy`), patient pages 86, Today's visit 83, Appointments 75, Cycle / IVF 73, Messages 66, Stock 64, Pain 52, Me 47, the exams 43, everything else 208. Removing spacing would save 3% only. No single area dominates.
- **The bigger cost was how often it travels and what it left behind:**
  1. `phUpdateCheck` fetched the whole page at `?probe=<time>` with `cache:"no-store"` 20 s after opening, every 5 minutes, and each time the tab came back: 1.8 MB each time (about 22 MB an hour while open).
  2. sw.js's cache-first branch stored every probe: one 7–10 MB copy per check, kept until the gold Update activates a new worker (sandbox: 16, then 23 copies, 163 MB; +21 MB in seconds). The 2026-10-14 photo eviction came from disk pressure on a nearly full disk, so this likely contributed (not proven on her machine).
  3. sw.js fetched every navigation with `no-store`, so every open downloaded the full page even when nothing had changed.
- **Fixed:**
  - `phUpdateCheck`: one fixed address `PH_PROBE_URL` (`?probe=1`) with `cache:"no-cache"` (GitHub Pages answers an unchanged page with a 304 and no body); reads only the page's head (`phProbeHead`, stops at the stamp or 64 KB); sweeps stored probe copies out of LCM's own `lcm-` caches before and after (`phProbeSweep`), so an older worker still active on a device can neither answer from its cache nor pile copies up. The compare and the button logic are unchanged.
  - sw.js: `probe=` requests pass straight through (never cached); navigations use `no-cache` (it still asks the server every time, so the 2026-08-19 reason for the cache mode still holds); each page's offline copy sits under its own key (the app as "./", chart.html and intake.html under their own path; opening chart.html used to overwrite the app's offline copy).
- **When it takes effect:** the page part on her first open of the next build (the first check per open downloads once, then 304s); the sw.js part when she presses the gold Update (the new worker also deletes the old cache with every stored copy in it).
- **Tested** (sandbox port 8994, and live GitHub Pages): with the old worker active, 23 stored copies became 1 after a check and stayed 1 after a second; the check read 458 KB of the 10 MB page and stopped; a temporary page stamped 20991231-000000 revealed the gold Update button through the real `phUpdateCheck` text, and the same build did not; with the new worker activated, the app booted, "./" held the app, a check stored nothing, chart.html was kept under its own key with "./" still the app, and with the server stopped the app opened from its offline copy; Prescriptions search narrowed (Tess shown, Zara and Mona hidden) and returned; from a browser on GitHub Pages, the first ask was 1,809,175 bytes and the second 300 bytes. The temporary page was binned after.
- **Not tested:** her real devices (the Key2 on 4G, the clinic computer); a real new build arriving through the full Update flow; how many stored copies her devices hold now (that needs her Chrome).
- **Pages checked:** Appointments (boot), Prescriptions list and search, My Cycle (chart.html). Nothing on screen looks different.

Mock `herb-schedule-mock-2026-10-26.html` (Artifact "Herbal Schedule"), 12 popup picks, then "Yes": all three are hard (remembering, which and when, running out) · **set clock times, she types them, nothing pre-filled** ("i decide") · tick in all three places (calendar, Me drawer, Herbs page) · on the calendar **its own block** · due = **glows gold** until ticked · running low = **N days left + Dispense** · two formulas = **a row each** · a fasting day keeps the doses at her times · a late tick counts any time that day · a new prescription **takes over by itself, keeping her times**.
- **Which prescription** (`phHbRows`, derived on read, nothing copied): scripts on her own record (the My profile name). The scripts dispensed on her **latest dispense day** are the schedule, one row each (that is how "takes over" and "a row each" fit together: a dispense on a later day replaces the earlier set; two scripts dispensed the same day are two rows); nothing dispensed yet = her record's own script, from today. Dose text / instruction: `schedPrepDosageText` / `schedPrepInstructionText` (the stored-script reads); dose days: `phFuDayPredicate` (Days it cannot read = every day); runs out: that dispense's follow-up (`PHARMACY.followups`, the Follow-ups page's own date), else `phFollowupCalc`. Days left = dose days from today to that day; "Last day"; "Ran out <day>" (red); a fortnight after it ran out the row leaves.
- **Data (her Me row, both logins):** `d.hbt` = {sid: {id, at: ["HH:MM" | ""], up}} her times (a script with none of its own reads her latest set: a new prescription keeps her times); `d.hbk` = {"day|sid|i": {id, at ISO, up, del?}} a dose taken. Merged entry by entry (`phHbNorm` / `phHbMerge` / `phHbAhead` beside the fasts in `phMeNormData` / `phMeMerge` / `phMeAhead`).
- **Where:** a **Herbs** step in the Mine group after Fasting (`RANK` 7.65; count "1/2" beside it, `phHbRailMini`) = `phHbPageHtml`: a card per prescription (jar, name, dose · instruction, days left + **Dispense** = her prescription open on Dispense), Times (time fields; on a phone without the clock icon so both sit on one line), Today (a chip per dose, tap = taken), Week (the last 7 days, today last, as the mock: a row per dose, filled = taken, dashed = not taken, a dash = no dose, "n of m"). **Me drawer:** a Herbs section under Today's meals, a tick per dose today, days left on the first row (`phHbDrwHtml`). **Grid:** each dose its own 15-minute block in her herb green `#15803D` with a leaf (`phHbDayItems` joins `phC22Src`; `phC22Ic` leaf; `phHbAct` / `phHbCls` in `phC22LifeHtml` and `phC22FoldHtml`): today's tap toggles taken with Undo, another day's opens its card (`phHbPopHtml`, also a stack's row); an untimed dose folds into the row above the day; on a phone outside the patients' hours they are the chips above / below. **⋯ menu:** Herbs beside Fasting. Every surface carries the same key (`data-ph-hb-tk`); a write repaints them all (`phHbRepaint`: `phMeRepaint(true)`, the page, the rail) and pops the ticked one; a dose turns gold in place the minute its time comes (30 s timer, no repaint). A time typed while its field has focus is saved quietly and the page repaints when she leaves the field (Enter saves at once): no repaint under her typing, no jump from one time box to the next.
- **Colours:** taken = `--ph-good`; due = a gold ring (`--ph-gold`, her pick); days left = `--ph-low` amber, ran out = `--ph-zero`; blocks = her herb green. Motion only on a change (`.pop`) and the due glow; all off under reduced motion.
- **Tested** (sandbox 8994, a made-up record "Ann Herbtest" as My profile, Gui Pi Tang 3 spoons twice a day Mon–Fri, dispensed Fri 23 Oct, 90 g): runs out Thu 5 Nov, "9 days left" (counted by hand too); typed 8:00 / 20:00 (saved, toast with Undo); a new script id kept the times; 8 am glowed gold at 10:23 and its tick turned it green (rail 1/2, "1 of 4" over the 7 days, Friday's two dashed), Undo, untick; the drawer ticks (2 of 2) and the grid repaint; ten blocks Mon–Fri on the week grid at 1280 (scaled to fit), today's tap = taken, gold when due; another day's card (8:00 pm · Dose 2 of 2 · Tue 27 Oct); phone 375: the page (no sideways scroll, times on one line after the fix), the chips above / below the day, a tap; Dispense opened her prescription on Dispense; ⋯ menu lists Herbs; the quiet time save (same field, still focused) then the repaint on leaving; Prescriptions search 3 → "Zed" 1 → 3. No console errors.
- **Not tested:** a dose inside a stack of 4+ (its row opens the same card through phC22PopHtml, code path only); her real data and her real prescription (which formula, whether she logs her own dispenses: with none logged the schedule uses her record's own script from today and shows no days left); two devices through the cloud row; the gold turning on by itself at the minute (the timer's code path only); a real phone's time picker.
- **Integration checked:** Herbs page, Me drawer, Appointments grid (week + phone day), a dose's card, the rail, the ⋯ menu, Dispense. Not shown elsewhere on purpose: the Mine hub's Week journal, Fasting, the Diet page.

## A smaller meal card (2026-10-26)
- **Her ask** (screenshot of the Break Fast card with + Food open, a sideways scrollbar along its bottom): "improve this display so it is more space saving".

  5. B: no "Planned" word; the Just today | Every <meal> bar sits under the time
  6. B: Had it and Edit on one row (Had it twice as wide)
  7. B: no count beside FOOD / DRINKS
  8. B: the cup only where food and drinks mix (the open list, the calendar, the Diet page), none under Drinks
- **Built** (`index.html`): `phMealListHtml` (chips `.ph-meal-it`, a dish's name a `data-meal-dish` button, `phMealNatDot` for its nature dot), `phMealListPickHtml` (`.ph-meal-lpk`: `.ph-meal-own` field + "+ New", `.ph-meal-chs` of `.ph-meal-ch` chips, `data-meal-n` on each for the narrowing), `phMealCardHtml` (no Planned label; Edit inside `.ph-meal-acts` while planned, its own row after Had it), the input handler narrows `[data-meal-n]`. CSS: the list block rewritten at TAPPABLE THINGS sizes (32px, 6px, 1px line, 13px); `.ph-meal-pick` gets `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)` (the snack picker too); `.ph-meal-acts .solid` grows 2; `.ph-meal-fastn + .ph-meal-bar` keeps its gap on a fast night. Removed as dead: the `.ph-meal-prow.on` / `.in` / `button.ph-meal-prow` rules (only the old list rows used them). `phMealDotIn` stays for the Diet page's lines.
- **Tested** (sandbox 8995, real clicks and the real handlers): closed 360px, open 506px (was ~510 / 736), scrollWidth = width (no sideways scroll); a dish chip adds it (solid, the list stays open, the toast's Undo); typing "coc" hides Meat Pie; "Toast" + Enter adds own:Toast and keeps the field focused; Done closes; ✕ removes Eating out; the latte's name opens its Drink editor and Save returns to the card; Every Breakfast makes the day's list her usual; Had it → "Meat Pie … + 2" with Undo, then Had it | Edit back on one row; her usual-meal sheet (no Skipped) and a patient's Diet sheet (Skipped, Same as usual) render the same chips; 360px phone sheet fits (336 = 336). **What it is:** `yangBody` in `PH_PP` (the mock's `YangPic` on PH_PP's own helpers): the Her build person (`anat`, now with `{ s, y0, h }`
so it can draw at 212/466 in a 300 x 252 frame) with three fires (Ming Men between the kidneys, the Spleen fire, the Heart fire), warmth
flowing up the trunk, out the arms and down the legs; Yang deficiency = the fires low and frosted, the flow short and slow, cold climbing
from the hands and feet, a cold belly and back, a pale face and lips, puffy ankles, clear urine falling, a slow heart that skips every

## Phone calendar: Google's spacing (2026-10-27)

Her ask: "improve my mobile ui calendar view, it feels too squished. use google calendar mobile as a guide for spacing.

`calendar-phone-spacing-mock-2026-10-27.html` (artifact T4BzKuua1H7xkV5mkjWLou, names fictional), her 9 picks then "Yes,
build it": 1 B one toolbar row · 2 A one date row · 3 A time column 64px, 11px hours · 4 A 3px gap · 5 A name first, 2
lines · 6 B text inset stays 7px · 7 A an hour stays 66px · 8 A no card · 9 A Saved pill shows 3 s.

Built, phone only (≤640px; the computer and tablet widths untouched):

  Me · 🔍. The date ▾ is a `.ph-atb-dd` whose menu holds the day counts (same `data-ph-apptcal-days` buttons), the
  Grid | List segment and Both clinics. 🔍 / ✕ are `data-ph-apptcal-srch="1|0"` (click handler beside the nav one):
  open adds `.srch` (the row shows only the search box, focused); ✕ clears `phApptCalQ` and repaints. `phApptCalSrch`
  keeps it open through the repaints typing makes.
- `phApptCalGridHtml`: `phone` / `one` (phone + 1 day). Gutter 64px on a phone. `one`: the head has no gutter cell; the
  day label (MON + date) sits in the time column, `.ph-apptcal-hd1` holds `phC22FoldRowHtml("before", …, bare=true)`
  (the one day's `.ph-c22-fd` cell, its ▴ inside when open), the fast chip and the CD chip (right). The separate "before"
  fold row is skipped; the trip row and the "after" row stay.
- CSS (PHONE REDESIGN block, "the calendar with Google Calendar's spacing"): wrap `margin: 0 -12px`, no border or
  radius, white; head / body / fold / trip rows `padding-right: 13px` (blocks end 16px from the edge), a `::after` on
  the grid carries the hour lines to the edge; hours 11px body font, `right: 12px`; the selected-day underline moved to
  `.hd1` (to the screen edge). Gap: blocks and her events get a transparent 1px top + right border with
  `background-clip: padding-box` on top of the grid's own 2px (the white seam ring stays, overlapping blocks still part).
  Name first: `.lg` blocks are a wrapping flex (name 100%, then the time, then the focus line with a "·" before it);
  sm / xs reorder their one line (name, then time; a narrow column drops the time whole: `:not(.lg) .r1` wraps at 18px);
  the herbs "!" moves to the block's top-right. Her events: name 14px / 600, time 12px; a tall one (time on its own
  line, `:has(> .tm)`) clamps the name to two lines. Selectors carry `.ph-apptcal-daycol` so they outrank the spacing
  audit's later rules.

  her pick's effect already holds and lengthening it to 3 s would cover the blocks longer. Told her; 3 s on her word.

## Came in for: edit in Details, any number of Mains, a sign on the bar (2026-10-27)
Her synth22 batch (closed with "fiinshed"): (1) the Compass header "From Baseline | Last visi" was cut; (2) "how to have more
than one main complaint"; (3) "how to choose if a sign can be tracked with the bar like complaints"; (4) "or select the sign as a
complaint too"; (5) "how to edit the chief complaint and complaints". One plan, mock `complaints-batch-mock-2026-10-27.html`
(artifact TEhyLsTvSsSYYgj491pf2J), her 8 picks, all the recommended ones, then "Yes, build it". Built in the order 1, 5, 2, 4, 3.
- **Header (item 1, no question):** the cut could not be made to happen at 360 / 1024 / 1160 / 1280 / 1440, so it is locked: a
  switch never shrinks (`.ph-cx-hd .ph-cx-sw { flex: none }`, nowrap words; `overflow: hidden` on a flex item let it shrink and
  clip), and From · the switches · Chart ▾ sit in one `.ph-cx-tools` group that moves down a line together.
- **Details on every row (Q4 Details ▾ in the panel, Q5 Name · How long · ★ Main · Remove):** `phCxCcFormHtml` for a typed
  complaint (the chief too), the pain's own form for a pain, `phCxSxTrackHtml` for a sign; the narrow card's drawer carries the
  same form. Name and How long save on change and update in place (`phCcWrite`; a tap that ends the typing is never lost); How
  long reads `phCcParseDatePrec` like the pain form. Remove on a secondary = `phCxRemoveSec` (Undo); on the chief =
  `phCxRemoveMain`: the next complaint (a Main one first) takes the slot with its own scores, notes, baseline and Goal (ccTrack
  `sec[id]` moves to `main`), none left = the slot empties and Came in for reads the pain map / plan again; Undo restores both
  records.
- **Any number of Mains (Q1 any number, Q3 each Main first in its own group, groups with a Main first):** `star` on every item
  (`phCxItems`): the chief's is `!c.mainOff`, a secondary's `s.main`, a pain's `p.main` (with no pain starred, the pain that
  carries a hidden chief shows Main by `st.chiefStar`). `main` still means the chief's slot (key, family, Goal), which never
  moves, so every complaint keeps its own scores. `phCxStarToggle` is the one switch (the panel, the drawer, the pain form, the
  Musculoskeletal pain table through `phPmSetMain`, which no longer clears the other pains or overwrites a typed chief); one
  complaint always stays Main ("One complaint stays Main"). The old table's ★ (`phCcSecPromote`) is the same switch now: its
  2026-10-15 swap left the score history with the slot, not the complaint (fixed on the way).
- **One-line places (Q2 every Main joined):** `phCxMainsOf` / `phCxCcMulti` / `phCxAlsoOf`; with more than one Main (or a Main
  that is not the chief) the Care Plan's Came in for row reads "★ Poor sleep + Headaches · Bloating", Aim "poor sleep and
  headaches", Watch a "main" line per Main, `phCcFillAim` addresses every Main; with one Main they read exactly as before. Copy
  notes has no Main line (it lists every score), so nothing changed there. The File search tags a Main secondary "Main".
- **A sign's two doors (Q6 both, Q7 stays in its Signs line, Q8 stays ticked + Sign tag):** Track with Better · Same · Worse |
  Bar 0–10 (`phCxSxTrack`, `rec.ccTrack.sxBar[signKey] = { id, at }`, back = `{ id, off }` so its bar scores return with it);
  on the bar it is scored like a complaint under `s:<id>` (its first bar score is its baseline), drawn after its group's
  complaints with its Sign tag (`.sxbar`), its earlier ratings under "Before" in Details, its pills row hidden (`phCxSignList`);
  no Goal (the Care Plan Goal skips it), never a pain (`phCxPainDup`). Make it a complaint (`phCxSignToComplaint`, now in
  Details too) keeps a bar sign's id and scores, leaves the Fang Bing Ren tick, and the complaint wears a small Sign tag;
  Remove drops the complaint and the sign row comes back.

Her words: "include a other option to add unusual conditions in medical history". Mock `hx-other-mock-2026-10-27.html`
(Artifact "History Other Condition"), her 4 picks, all A, then "Yes, build it". Built: `shots/hx-other-built-desktop-2026-10-27.png`,

**Her picks:** 1 A "+ Other condition" at the end of General health: type, Add, it is its own Yes row (Added tag, ✕ removes it) with
its note; 2 A the same at the end of Family history (blood relatives); 3 A the patient's history link gets "+ Something else" and it
arrives as an Added Yes row with the patient's words, tagged Form; 4 A a typed condition shows everywhere a Yes shows.
**Code (index.html):** `phHxOtherItems` (the typed rows that are Yes, oldest first), `phHxWithOther` (puts them where their group
ends; `phHxApplicableItems` and the figure's `phHxItems` read it), `phHxOtherFind` (a list row of the same words and kind, else a
typed row of that name), `phHxOtherPut` (Yes on that row, making the typed row when there is none), `phHxOtherFromForm`,
`phHxOtherRemove` (returns the Undo), `phHxOtherRowHtml` / `phHxOtherAddHtml` / `phHxOtherCommit` beside `phHxBodyHtml`; taps
`data-hx-oadd` / `data-hx-ook` / `data-hx-orm` before `data-hx-set`; Enter / Esc on `data-hx-oin` (a window capture listener, so
Esc closes the box and not the history sheet); view state `presHxOtherAdd`. CSS `.ph-hx-orow`, `.ph-hx-otag`, `.ph-hx-orm`,
`.ph-hx-oadd`, `.ph-hx-oadd-box`, `.ph-hx-ook` (beside the group-note rules). The herb caution (`phClinicalFlag`) matches a typed
condition on its own words (4 letters or more), own or family, as the list's family rows already do.
**The link:** intake.html `otherRows` / `otherAddRow` / `otherRenderRows` (Condition + Details, ×), sent as `history.others = [{ n,
f: 1 = family, note }]` (20 at most; a plain key on the jsonb blob, no SQL); a resend brings the rows back with their details. The
app sends `prefill.others` = the conditions the PATIENT wrote before (`src: "form"`, names only); her own typed conditions and every
note stay in the app. Review: a new one = "X: Yes (added by the patient) · details"; one on file as a Yes only brings details its
note lacks; a list row of the same words answered No or Don't know is a Keep / Use new choice (key `other-<i>`: the choice buttons
split their key on ":"); the same condition twice on one form is listed once.

## The freeze on load (2026-10-27)
Her report: "the app has been freezing and taking a long time to load on the desktop - find out how to resolve this".
- **Seen:** her LCM window (the installed app, Chrome) sat on "Loading your pharmacy..." under Chrome's "Page Unresponsive";
  its page process used a whole core and grew 660 → 776 MB. The live build in a Chrome tab froze the same way. The sandbox
  (made-up data) started in 2 s, so it was her records.
- **How it was found (read-only, reusable for the next freeze):**
  - Host: a same-site page outside every app's scope with no security rule (the C6 icon,
    `b00k33.github.io/c6-jingfang/assets/favicon-32.png`). Any `/lcm-pharmacy/` address opens in her app window instead,
    and GitHub's 404 page blocks scripts.
  - The probe: her installed build's text (from the `lcm-` cache) written into a frame on that page. Every save went to a
    memory copy, IndexedDB and cache writes were no-ops, sending was blocked, sync was off, the worker was not registered.
  - Every loop head and function entry was counted. Every 300 ms a short progress note (counts and the call chain, no
    records) was written to `zzprobe-trail`, read after the frozen tab was ended, then removed.
  - Scripts: scratchpad build9 probe2.js to probe4.js.
- **Cause:** a circle among the written-from-the-record summaries:
  - The booking brief asks the Care Plan for its goal (`phApptBrief` → `phTpAutoGoal`, 10-10).
  - The goal reads the complaints (`phCxItems` → `phCcRibItems` → `phCcAuto`, 10-21).
  - The complaints read each open plan's pain map (`phPmList`).
  - A plan with no saved pain map asks the booking brief for its complaint (`phPmComplaint` → `phApptBrief`), and around
    again.
  - Each overflow was caught (`try`/`catch` in `run` and `phCcAuto`) and the next plan tried, so it branched once per open
    plan. With her records (670 patients, 99 with plans, about 800 prescriptions) a turn outlasted the 1.5 s memo window,
    the memo emptied, and it never settled. On smaller data it settled, slowly.

## Care Plan part 2, step 4: course length from the patient (2026-10-27)

Her pick 5 ("How long" chips at the door; a longer history adds visits to the first two phases), mock

- **One fact:** the chips are the main concern's own How long (`complaint.since`, the Came in for row's box), not a second
  answer. `phCcLenBand(since)` = the band by whole months back: under 2 = Weeks, under 6 = Months, under 12 = 6–12 months, under
  36 = 1–3 years, else Longer. A chip writes 3 weeks / 3 months / 9 months / 2 years / 5 years back as a "~" worked-out date
  (`phCcMainSinceSet(iso, false, true)`, which repaints Came in for and the door); the chip of the band her own date is already
  in does nothing, so a typed date is never overwritten by its own band. The Weeks / Months line (2 months) is mine; both add 0.
- **The door** (`phTpDoorStartHtml`, under Came in for): "How long" + the five chips (32 px, the lit one solid), then Start, now
  "Course · Low back pain · 3 phases · 9 visits" (the course's planned visits with the band's extra).
- **The course** (`phTpCourseLenApply`): when a course starts (`presTpInlineCreate`: the door and "+ New"; `phTpCreate`) or is
  swapped (Change course → Swap the phases), the band adds visits to phase 1 / phase 2: 6–12 months +1 / 0, 1–3 years +1 / +1,
  Longer +2 / +2 (the mock's table: Low back pain 7 → 8 → 9 → 11). Only a phase that has a count gets more. Cycle courses
  (`PH_TP_CYCLE_TEMPLATES`) keep theirs: they follow the calendar. Written once into `phase.sessions`, hers to change after.

  14 logged visits; 15 of 40 course plans past their phase's planned visits and still in it. Reading the code: bookings
  already counted (`phTpPhaseSessionDates`, `phTpPhaseVisitStats`); the move lived only in the session-log save hook.
- **The card** (`phTpPrvCtx` / `phTpPrvHtml`): shows when the visits before today + today reach the planned count, whether or
  not today is logged (part 2 hid it once today was logged, because the log carried out the pick). Nothing is pre-picked (part
  2 had Move solid). `ctx.last` = the date of the planned-th visit (today when it is today's).
- **The tap** (`phTpPrvDo`, the click handler on `data-tp-prv-pick`): Stay = `ph.sessions` + half again, review "Staying 2 more
  visits"; Move = `phTpPhaseStatusData(plan, next, "current")`, review "Moved to Subacute", and when the planned-th visit was
  before today the old phase's `doneKey` = that day and the next phase's `sinceKey` = the day after (so the visits since count
  for the next phase); Close (last phase) = plan done, phase `doneKey` today. Each review carries `prv.undo` ({v, sessions}).
  Then `savePharmacy()` + `renderPresPanel()` (keeps the scroll).
- **Undo** (`data-tp-prv-undo`, `phTpPrvUndo`): removes that review; Stay puts the old count back; Move makes the old phase
  current again (`phTpPhaseStatusData`, later phases upcoming); Close reopens the plan and the phase.
- **Logging a visit** (the `data-pres-acu-log` save) no longer moves the plan, writes a review or sets `phTpAutoAdv`; the
  card stays until her tap. The Treatment tab banner code for `phTpAutoAdv` is left in place, unreached.

## Care Plan part 3, step 5: the cycle review (2026-10-27)

Her pick 5 and her ask28 answer "At her next booking" (not when the period is logged). Mock section 5. Measured: 26 cycle plans
(22 with an LMP, 8 with cycle day logs); 9 of 12 had a period in the last 90 days. Already there: the cycle history table
(`phCycleHistoryHtml`: starts from `phBbtCycleStarts`, flow / pain from `rec.cycleLog`).

- **`phCycRvModel(rec, plan)`**: an active cycle-template plan with three or more starts. `st[k]` is the period that began the
  cycle she is in; the cycle that just ended is `st[k-1]`..`st[k]`, the one before `st[k-2]`..`st[k-1]`. Each: length in
  days, the period's `flowIntensity` and `pain` from its `cycleLog` entry, `clot` = the most clots on its days
  (`phCycClots` of `rec.cycleSigns[d]`: many 3, large 2, small 1).

  `.tg` tags of the review card.

  HEAD copy: `perl food.pl index.html rows.js sf.js 20261028`).

  `PH_SF_URL` (the worker then keeps it, cache-first, for offline). `phSfHtml` puts a **Shops** block under her own foods while

## Fang Bing Ren: search a formula (2026-10-28)
- **Her words** (screenshot of the formula blocks + the "Looking at" line): "i need to be able to search a formula from the fang
  bing ren list". Built straight in (a search on an existing box; no layout change; the blocks' masonry still waits for her word).
- **How:** the "Looking at" search box (placeholder now "Search signs or formulas"; the old "Search signs, or add a complaint"
  would be cut on her screen with the longer wording, and "+ Add as complaint" still shows once she types) also finds formulas.
  `phFbrFormMatch(q)`: 2+ letters, capitals and spaces ignored, a match from the start of any word of the name ("chai hu",
  "wen dan", "hu tang") or the initials ("xcht", "XC", "dcqt").
  - The blocks keep their place: found ones wear a 2px herb ring (`.fq-hit`), the rest fade to .35 (`.fq-miss`), never hidden;
    toggled in place on each keystroke (input handler), and drawn by `mosaicTile` on a repaint.
  - Under the box a **Formulas** chip row (`.ph-fbr-fq`, chips `.ph-fbr-fqc` 32px / 6px / 13px, herb dot + name + fit %), best fit
    first (`ranked`). A chip (`data-fbr-fqp`) looks at that formula (sets `phTriFilt`, never toggles it off; Pick several adds),
    empties the box, so its signs show. Enter in the box = the first chip. Tapping a block the search found also empties the box.
  - Words that find a formula and NO sign leave the signs as they are (`csOn` false; no "No matching signs here."); words that
    find both keep the sign search ("chai hu" finds 1 sign + 4 formulas).
- **Tested** (sandbox, made-up patient "Test Searchpatient", a few ticks, an MSK plan): "wen dan", "xcht", "XC", "chai hu" (4 chips,
  5 rings: Da Chai Hu Tang sits in two cards), "bloat" (8 signs, no formula row), "w" (nothing); chip, Enter and block each set the
  filter + empty the box; a sign search kept by a block tap; focus and caret stay while typing; 1280 (box 298px, placeholder needs
  ~190px) and 360 (chips wrap, page not wider, placeholder fits the 278px box); no console errors beyond the sandbox CDN 404s.
  Picture: shots/fbr-formula-search-2026-10-28.png.

  - Rows: label column 74px (sentence case 12px), every joined bar fills its line (`.ph-cs-grid .ph-ck-chips.seg`, 32px with its
    line, 13px). `phCsFit` (MutationObserver + resize, the `phPpScan` pattern) folds a bar too long for its line into an even
    joined grid: 2 rows, then 2 rows with the pictures dropped (`.bare`; a colour keeps its dot), then 3 or 4; its last cell spans
    what is left of its row. The 0–10 bar never folds. At her 643px card Discharge (4+3) and Pain type (3+2) fold; on a phone most do.

    the "today's pick / usual" legend became a small key at the head's right (`phCycDayHeadHtml(..., key)`), which also puts a dot
    in the phase's colour before "CD n · phase" (`.ph-cyc-phd`, the cycle picture's colours) in every day head.
  - How bad: one joined 0–10 bar (`.ph-cs-n10`, `data-cycle-painn`, a click handler beside Painful?'s): a tap sets the score (and
    the derived word), her score again clears it, cells below it pale; a half step from the old slider shows on its nearest cell.
    The slider stays in the older popover. The womb stays beside the bar (hidden on a phone).
  - PMS & mood: three bars, Mood (Irritable, Low mood) · Gut (Bloating, Loose stool, Constipation, Nausea) · Body (the rest, so a
    new option lands there). Other (Unprotected sex, Ovulation twinge) is one joined bar too.
  - BBT: − and + 32px circles either side of one tinted field (reading + °C, no spinner), the time a tinted field, Discard a chip.
    The Note is a tinted field. Fang Bing Ren's strip moved out of the second column to a band at the card's foot.
  - The rail: `.ph-cs-q::before` joins each number to the next, herb once that step is answered; hidden after the last step of a
    column on a wide (two-column) card.
  - Picked chips stay `--ph-herb-deep` here: the Cycle page's day box, footer and card share that rule (`:is(.cp-box, .cp-foot,
    .cp-card .cp-log...)`), so the card matches its page rather than the mock's lighter shade.

## Publish script: the publish commit is the stamp and nothing else (2026-10-28)
- **Why:** `publish-live.sh` checked the tracked tree was clean, ran the slow `git fetch`, then `sed -i` + `git add index.html
  sw.js` on the shared working copy. An edit another session made in that window went live inside the publish: 136b4716
  (build 20261028-143700) carried the unfinished muscle-marks build (its fixes are ad3097c0). fb6afe77 was clean because it
  was a hand publish under the lock (plumbing, no `git add`); `.git/worktrees/publish-wt` is only an empty leftover from 10/5.
- **Now:** the new index.html / sw.js come from session-a's committed blobs (`git cat-file blob <base>:<file>` through the
  same sed, `git hash-object -w --stdin`), staged with `git update-index --cacheinfo` in a private index
  (`.git/lcm-publish-index.<pid>`), and re-checked against the base before committing: only index.html and sw.js, modes
  unchanged, one line each, exactly the old and new stamp lines. `git commit-tree -p <base>`, then `git update-ref
  refs/heads/session-a <new> <base>` moves the branch only if no one committed meanwhile; the push is `<new>:refs/heads/main`
  (a fast-forward, never forced), so a commit made during the run does not ride along. After that the shared index entries
  move to the new blobs (only where still the base's), and the working copy gets the new value written at the stamp's byte
  offset (same length, nothing else rewritten; a stamp someone changed is left alone). The clean-tree rule is gone (open
  edits stay local; the dry run lists them); something staged still stops it. A base already carrying the next stamp (a
  publish whose push was rejected) stops with its own message.
- **Clock:** Git Bash has no zoneinfo, so `TZ=Australia/Sydney` meant UTC and the stamp fell back to "live + 1 minute"
  (143700 at 19:00). Now the POSIX rule `AEST-10AEDT,M10.1.0,M4.1.0/3` (checked across both daylight-saving changes).
- **Tested** in a scratch bare origin + clone (never GitHub): dry run; `--yes` with open edits in index.html (beside the
  stamp line and mid-file) and sw.js: the publish commit is 2 files, 1+ 1- each, the edits stay, the stamps are written in
  place. STOP cases: something staged; HEAD on another branch; a commit landing just before `update-ref` (nothing pushed);
  a sed that touched another line (caught by the re-check); main moved on (push rejected, nothing forced); session-a already
  carrying the next stamp. Another session staging sw.js mid-run: its staged entry kept. A hand-changed working stamp: left
  alone. A writer rewriting index.html all through a run: the commit still stamp-only and every line it wrote kept (its
  whole-file rewrite can replace the in-place stamp, which then shows as a local change, as before). Real repo: dry run only.
- **Not done:** no `--yes` on the real repo; that waits for her "push live".

## Meals: a meal she had can be edited (2026-10-28)
Her words, with a screenshot of the planner's Mon 26 Dinner ("7:50 pm · had it · Spicy Salmon Fishbowl"): "why cant i edit the spicy
salmon fishbowl?". Why: Had it keeps the meal as it was (`had.v`), and the cell shows that, but the picker read and wrote the day's
plan (`phMealPlan` / `e.v`). The Fishbowl came in from C22's log as her own words with its own numbers (`had.nut`) and no plan, so the
picker opened on "Same as every dinner" with her usual dinner (or nothing), and any change went to the plan while the cell kept
showing the Fishbowl.
- Fix: `phMealList` gives a meal she had (her own, a day, not Skipped) as `{ v: had.v, own, had }`; `phMealListPut` sends it to the new
  `phMealHadPut` (writes `had.v` only, toast + Undo as before); `phMealDayTopHtml` draws no day line for it ("Same as every …" and
  "<Day> only ↺ Undo" are about the plan). One read and one write, so the planner's picker, her meal card, − / +, Eating out and the
  ✕ all follow. `phDietSum`: C22's numbers cover her own words (`own:`); a food or dish added to such a meal counts its own; the
  numbers go when the last of her own words is taken out. Skipped on a had meal is unchanged (`phMealHadSet(…, "skip")`).
- **Tested** (sandbox `_meal-test.html`, a made-up "Zz Meal Edit" as My profile, a sandbox owner tag, Mon 26 Dinner seeded as C22
  brings it: `own:Spicy Salmon Fishbowl` with numbers; at 1280): the cell reads as in her screenshot; its picker lists Spicy Salmon
  Fishbowl with ✕, + Add, Eating out | Skipped, Done; + 1 cup white rice → cell "Spicy Salmon Fishbowl · 1 cup white rice", toast
  "✓ Dinner · Mon 26 Oct · + 1 cup white rice", numbers = C22's + the rice's, the day's plan untouched; ✕ Fishbowl → cell "1 cup white
  rice", C22's numbers gone; Undo brings it back; a meal not had (Thu 29) still writes the plan; Prescriptions search narrows and

## 2026-10-29 · Formula refill: choose how much to make
- **Her words** (screenshot of the weighing panel, "Weigh 140 g of Chai Hu Jia Long Gu Mu Li Tang", Jar 10 → 150 g): "how do i
  choose how much to make? sometimes i make 150 or 300 or 275". There was no way: Make always weighed the plan's batch
  (`phRefillBatchFor`: the recipe × the supplier pack), and the old batch dropdown (`data-ph-refill-batch`) left the row in the
  10/27 redesign.
- **Built (my call, the number she wants to change is where she reads it):** the grams in the heading are a field
  (`.ph-rfc-wgg field-bare`, `data-rfc-mk-g`; 32px, 6px, the field tint). A tap picks the whole number, so typing replaces it.
  Each keystroke re-weighs the list in place (`phRfcMkGrams` swaps the ring, the count, the jar line, the bowl, the rows and
  Finish; the field itself stays, so typing never stops), the ticks start over, and Enter or leaving the field keeps it as the
  formula's planned batch (`h.refillBatch`, the field the plan already had; Finish clears it as before). An empty or 0 entry
  goes back to the amount before.
- **Whole grams (her 2026-08-25 spec, her scale reads whole grams):** a batch that is a whole multiple of the recipe weighs
  exactly as before. Any other amount (150 or 275 of a 140 g recipe) splits into whole grams, the grams left over going to the
  herbs nearest their next gram, so the bowl and the scale's last reading are exactly the batch (`phRfcMkNums`). Finish
  deducts those same whole grams and adds the batch to the jar (before, a free amount would have shown 29.46 g).
- **Tested** (sandbox, a made-up 140 g recipe of 11 herbs, its jar at 10 g on To make): real click + typing 275 → rows 29 · 39
  · 10 · 20 · 20 · 29 · 10 · 20 · 20 · 39 · 39 = 275, "Jar 10 → 285 g", "Finish · add 275 g", the field kept focus; two ticks
  then typing 300 → ticks back to 0, rows add to 300; a tap on a herb row straight after typing saved 300 AND ticked the row;
  Not now → Make reopens at 300; tick all → Finish: log entry 300 g, every herb a whole gram, 300 g deducted, jar 10 → 310,
  the plan cleared; 280 (× 2) = the recipe doubled exactly; 150 → whole grams adding to 150; empty / 0 + Enter → back to the
  amount before; 375 px: the heading wraps, nothing cut, no sideways scroll. Picture: shots/refill-batch-grams-2026-10-29.png.
- **Integration (★★★):** the batch is the same `h.refillBatch` the row's Make, the week tiles' "short" counts and the short bar
  read (they repaint when it is kept). The bench's own Make × dropdown (`renderRefMultiplier`) is unchanged.
  Not checked: the Key2; her real recipes.

## 2026-10-29 · Sync guard: an older copy can't replace bookings, follow-ups or stock (live incident; her "Yes, fix it and push live") — LIVE build 20261029-161800 (carried by the Blood tests publish e6c93e61)
- **What happened** (measured read-only in her Chrome; her answer: "My phone"): between 3:42 and 3:52 pm her phone's copy,
  last synced about 1 October, won a merge and replaced the whole `pharmacy_core`: bookings 290 → 95 (200 gone, 27 upcoming,
  16 in the next 7 days), herb follow-ups 71 → 16 (55 gone, 17 Sep – 29 Oct), 83 herbs' stock amounts, the last stocktake
  (20 Oct → 16 Sep), the label template, sign links, two prepared messages. Patients survived (merged one by one,
  `mergePatientsByRecency`); the dispense log survived (its own section). Cause: `mergeSections` picks `pharmacy_core` WHOLE;
  on a conflict (both sides changed) it keeps the device's own copy, and `sectionLooksEmptier` only counted herbs and patients,
  so a stale copy with the same counts passed. No code change of the day touched bookings or follow-ups (checked 36176f34,
  81514da3, a05d9e8d, 02b8c148, 44a99ce3).
- **The good copy:** her browser's `lcmbak-daily` (15:42) holds 290 / 71; copied untouched to a new IndexedDB database
  `lcm-rescue-2026-10-29` (store `kv`, key `daily-1542`, the whole backup entry) on the b00k33.github.io origin, which the app never
  reads. **Data NOT repaired — her answer "Not now".** A repair = restore that copy's core, keep since 3:42: one refill (5 herbs
  deducted), one stock arrival, 5 new bookings, 2 patient edits; then verify the CLOUD row. Her phone must be on this build first.
- **Built:** `coreKeep(str)` (bookings count, follow-ups count, newest follow-up time; memo of 4 strings) + `coreDay`; in
  `sectionLooksEmptier`'s `pharmacy_core` branch: bookings ≥ 10 dropping under half, follow-ups ≥ 10 dropping under half, or the
  newest follow-up 14+ days older with at least 3 fewer = guarded (keep the fuller copy, the existing `showSyncNote`, now worded
  "looked emptied out or out of date"). Bookings only grow (the paste adds, no prune since 2026-09-10) and shrink one by one;
  follow-ups shrink one per deleted dispense, so these never trip on her own work.
- **Tested** (sandbox, the guard's own source pulled from the file): the incident's numbers trip (290 → 95 bookings); the reverse
  passes; one booking deleted, the newest dispense deleted (newest 10 days older), 2 fewer follow-ups with an old newest, a small
  clinic's 8 → 2 bookings all pass; an older copy with 60 of 71 follow-ups and a 20-day-older newest trips; an unreadable copy
  trips; herbs and the log keep their old checks; the app boots with the sync loaded and no console errors. **Not tested:** a
  real two-device merge (needs her logins).

## 2026-10-29 · Plans close themselves: the last planned visit asks once, then the plan finishes itself (not live)
Her pick 15 from the patient-profile audit (`patient-interactivity-audit-2026-10-29.html`; her answer 9 "Plans finish themselves"),
mock `plans-close-mock-2026-10-29.html` (A ask once then it closes itself · B closes with Done · C cycle plans end too), her 8
picks, all the recommended option: **A + C**. The gap: the gold review card (`phTpPrvCtx`) never showed on a cycle plan (32 of her
103) and came back on every visit after the last planned one; nothing ever set `plan.status = "done"` by itself (2 of 103 finished).
- **The ask, once, saying what happens untouched** (`phTpPrvHtml`): the last phase's card gained a fact line: "Nothing booked after
  today · closes itself tomorrow" / "Booked 5 Nov · closes itself after it" / "Kept open · closes itself the day after the next
  visit" (after her Undo of a close).
- **Closes itself** (`phTpSelfCloseSweep`, run inside `phTpSyncPlansOnOpen` when her file opens and again when Today's visit draws;
  `phTpSelfClose`): a plan whose last phase's planned visits are done, with nothing booked or logged after its last visit and no tap
  of hers since, closes the day after that visit, dated so (never the day the sweep ran): `plan.status = "done"`, `plan.closedKey`,
  `plan.selfClosed = {date, last, ph, planned, more, crs}`, the phase done, one review line "Closed itself · 10 visits over 12
  weeks" (`prv.auto`, with Undo). Today's card turns green "✓ Closed itself · …" with Undo and the Ending letter. The Care Plan band
  and the Treatment band say **Closed itself 30 Oct 2026 · 10 visits over 12 weeks · Reopen · 2 more visits · Ending letter**
  (`phTpSelfClosedHtml`); the Plans row says "closed 30 Oct 2026" on any closed plan (`plan.closedKey`, written by the card's Close
  plan and the ⋯ menu's Mark completed too; Reopen plan forgets a self-close).
- **Reopens itself** (`phTpSelfReopen`): a booking or a logged visit after the close reopens the newest self-closed plan (while no
  plan is active or paused) with N more visits (`phTpPrvStayN`, as Stay does; a cycle plan: another cycle), the phase current again,
  one review line "Reopened · 2 more visits · closed itself 30 Oct 2026"; Today's card: "✓ Reopened · 2 more visits" · "Subacute ·
  visit 5 of 6 · closed itself 30 Oct 2026" · Undo · New course instead (undoes the reopen and opens the new-plan cards on the Care
  Plan tab). **An Undo holds:** undo of a reopen keeps the plan closed until a booking after today (`selfClosed.held`); undo of a
  close keeps it open until a later visit (`plan.keepOpen`); her next tap on the card clears the hold. The app's own lines never
  count as her tap (`phTpPrvTouched` skips `prv.auto`), so a reopened plan still closes itself after its extra visits.
- **Cycle plans end too** (`phTpCycEndCtx`, `phTpCycCourse`, `phTpCycEndDo`): Natural fertility · PCOS · Endometriosis ·
  Dysmenorrhea · Amenorrhea: a course = cycles from the concern's How long (Weeks 1 · Months 3 · 6–12 months 6 · 1–3 years 12 ·
  Longer 12; no concern = 3; `PH_TP_CYC_COURSE`) + `plan.cyclesMore`; cycles done = period starts since the plan began
  (`phBbtCycleStarts`; the cycle it began in counts; Amenorrhea, or no cycle data, counts months). The last cycle's late days
  (luteal, or overdue) show "Cycle 3 of 3 done · 9 visits over 13 weeks" with the course table, **Close plan · Another cycle** (one
  more cycle, with Undo) and "closes itself after the next period"; the sweep closes it at the next period's start (or the day after
  a later visit), and the band offers "Reopen · another cycle". **IVF Protocol ends at the pregnancy test** (`phTpTestCtx`: the
  latest transfer's result, else her Pregnant? test, dated on or after the plan began): **🌸 Positive test 28 Oct 2026 · …** → Start
  Pregnancy plan (the due-date step, then the Pregnancy plan; the IVF plan closes with "Pregnancy plan started" only once that step
  finishes, Cancel leaves it) · Keep this plan (with Undo); **Negative test** → Another cycle (the IVF questions; this plan closes
  once they are answered) · Close plan; untouched, it closes the day after the test. A positive test on any cycle plan asks the
  same. The rail's "Review today" tag counts these cards too.
- Not built (her picks did not ask for them): B (closes with Done · Copy for Cliniko); a Timeline entry.

its fact line; the sweep on open closes a plan whose last visit was yesterday (green card, the band's line, the Plans row); a
booking today reopens it (card with the fact; Undo holds it closed and a second sweep leaves it; the band's Reopen opens it; New

## 2026-10-30 · Opens without internet
Her words: "i want it to operate without internet including opening" (after "can lcm app work if not connected to internet?").
The app already worked offline once open; opening was the problem. Measured on a copy of the app with the cloud cut off
(supabase-js retries a failed token refresh for ~26 s, postgrest retries a GET for ~8 s, and a failed refresh reports
INITIAL_SESSION with no session, which with the wifi up led to the sign-in wall):

| How it opens | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| No internet, signed in within the hour | 7.9 s on "Starting…" | 0.9–1.6 s, in on this device's copy |
| No internet, signed in longer ago | 26.3 s | 0.9–1.6 s |
| Wifi but no internet, signed in longer ago | the sign-in wall after 26 s (no password can pass offline) | 0.9–1.6 s |
| Wifi but no internet, recent sign-in | 7.9 s | 0.9–1.6 s |

**What changed** (all in the sync IIFE, above `function boot()`; sw.js SHELL):
- `openLocalNow(why)`: in on this device's copy (`goLocalOffline`) when it holds the pharmacy (`localReady`), never another
  login's copy (`storedEmail()` from the saved sign-in must match the `lcm-data-owner` tag); with the wifi up but no answer, only
  a device that has synced with this login before (`lcm-sync-base` present).
- `bootFetch`: the cloud client's own fetch (`createClient(..., { global: { fetch: bootFetch } })`). The first failed request
  before she is in opens the local copy; any answer sets `netAnswered`; once in on the local copy with the wifi up (no "online"
  event will come), the first good answer calls `resumeCloud()`.
- `boot()`: `!navigator.onLine` → `openLocalNow("offline")` at once; no answer for `OPEN_HANG_MS` (10 s) → `openLocalNow("net")`
  (a slow phone that does answer still boots online as before); getSession's "no session" goes local when `netFail(err)` says
  the network failed, not only when the browser says offline.
- `onAuthStateChange`: INITIAL_SESSION with no session is ignored (getSession decides); TOKEN_REFRESHED / SIGNED_IN while in on
  the local copy → `resumeCloud()`.
- `afterAuth()`: `openedLocal` (set by `goLocalOffline`) = no "Loading your pharmacy…" cover over her work, and the cloud
  answering late goes through `resumeCloud()`, **never `go()`**: `go()` sets `lastPushed` to the local data and would mark her
  offline edits as already sent.
- The online listener is now the named `resumeCloud()` (same body: reload if no client, record the session, subscribe,
  `pullMergePush(true)`). `ownerOk()` and every cloud-write gate are untouched.
- sw.js SHELL adds the sign-in library and the PDF reader (`pdf.min.mjs`, `pdf.worker.min.mjs`), so a new build opens and
  reads PDFs offline from its first open; the photo-text reader (tesseract, ~15 MB) stays online-only.

**Tested** on a copy of the app with a test script in its head (`mocks/offline-open-harness.html`, local only: `?m=off` no
network; `?m=lie` wifi up, the cloud unreachable; `?m=late&after=5000` unreachable for 5 s, then a pretend cloud answers;
nothing reaches the real cloud): all four cases above in 0.9–1.6 s with the offline chip, and no sign-in wall after the
library's retries end (~26 s); `late` with an expired sign-in: token refresh at ~7.1 s → `resumeCloud` → GET + POST settings,
no cover, "Saved"; `late` with a fresh sign-in: the GET retry lands at ~7.9 s → POST at 8.6 s; a healthy start makes the same
calls as the old build; a signed-out device online still shows sign-in; no console errors. sw.js: a fresh install's cache holds
the 8 shell files + the 3 jsdelivr files (CORS 200), and a reload loads `window.supabase` and `window.pdfjsLib` from the cache.
**Not tested:** her real devices, the Key2, a real network drop; the other-login refusal in `openLocalNow` (read, not driven).
LIVE 2026-10-30 on her "push live", build 20261031-005000 (publish commit df01684e).

## Emoji sweep (2026-10-31)
Her yes in the audit popup ("About 400 emoji are still on screens … Swap them for the app's own icons?" → "Yes, swap them").
Three commits: fda1bbd7 (part 1, 340), e83c739c (part 2, 76), ffec6568 (part 2b, 5). Scripts kept in the session scratchpad
(`emo-a.pl` classifier + map, `emo-b.pl` / `emo-c.pl` exact counted replacements).
**The rule applied:** an emoji in screen markup → its sprite icon, written `<svg class=icn aria-hidden=true><use href=#i-x></use></svg>`
(no quotes, so it is safe inside any JS string); an emoji in a plain-text spot (toast, flash, hover title, aria-label, dropdown
option, textContent, a Yes-label, an escaped or joined string) → dropped, its words kept. The map: ⚠ warn, 🌿🌱 leaf, 🏺🫙 jar,
🩸💧 drop, 📷🖼 camera, ✉📮📨 mail, 📦 parcel, 🧪🔬 pt-vial, 📋 clipboard, 💊 pill, 🛒 cart, 🖨 print, 🥚 egg, 🗑 trash, 🔄🔁
refresh, 🏠 home, 🧊 pt-snow, 🚗 car, 🔔⏰🕐 clock, 📅 cal, 💗💛🫀🌸 heart, ⚡ bolt, 🪡 needle, 😴🌙 moon, 🔥 pt-flame, 📝🖌 edit,
📜 scroll, 👅 pt-tongue, 🏷 tag, 📖📘📚🧭 book, 📍📌 pin, 📊📈 chart, 💰💳 coin, 👤👥🧍🦴 user, 🚫 no, 🚚 truck, 🙂😊 face, 🔗 link,
💬 msg, 📱 mobile, 🔍 search, ✋🧴 skin, ⚙ gear, 🛡🤧 shield, 💪 dumbbell, 📞 phone, 🎯 flag; Settings' Storage heading 💾 → doc.

## Trip program: the Plan tab becomes the week grid (2026-10-31)
Her words 2026-10-30: "i need to design a way for me to organise my trips where i have events that are trip related so i can
plan well. this is the program" (3 pictures of the 2026 Canada Jingfang Advanced Study Program, Nanjing), then "include travel
blocks and breakfast at 7am". Her 9 picks (all the recommended) on `trip-program-mock-2026-10-30.html`, "Yes, full mock first",
then "Yes, build it" on the full mock `trip-program-full-mock-2026-10-30.html` (artifact L8zebiis7bSAbcUP2Bsukb), which is
the contract.
**Built (all in the TRIPS block, index.html):**
- Data: a trip gains `venues [{id, n, nz, how, min}]` and `rules [{id, t, on "k:<kind>" | "v:<venue>"}]`; a plan row gains
  `k`, `sl` (am · pm · full · eve), `who` / `whoz`, `v`, `e`, `atz`, `note` (whitelist `PH_TRIP_PLAN_KEYS`, `phTripPlanSet`);
  `phTripSet` writes `v.<id>.x` / `r.<id>.x`; `phTripRowAdd` / `phTripRowDel` take `v` and `r`. Kinds `PH_TRIP_KINDS` (six of
  the program's + Mine), parts of the day `PH_TRIP_SLOTS`, reads `phTripKind`, `phTripSlot`, `phTripStart` / `phTripEnd`,
  `phTripWho`, `phTripVenue`, `phTripRules`. Breakfast is NOT a plan row: her Me meal (`phMealEvents(day).b`), a tap opens its
  card (`phRxCkOpen`).
- Desktop Plan (`phTripPlanHtml`): week bar (`phTripWeeks`, `phTripWkOf`), one solid Add, the grid (`phTripGridHtml`: breakfast
  · go · Morning · mid · Afternoon · back · Evening; a full day spans Morning to Afternoon; strip and breakfast rows only when
  filled; an empty cell = `data-trip-cell` and adds into that part, `phTripAddSl`), cards (`phTripCardHtml`), travel strips
  worked out on read (`phTripLegs`, `phTripStripHtml`, flights `phTripFlightsOn`), the open session (`phTripSesHtml`) or day
  (`phTripDayPanelHtml`), the folds (`phTripVenuesHtml`, `phTripRulesHtml`, `phTripFoldsHtml`; the Pack line opens Prepare's
  Pack area). Phone (`phTripPlanPhoneHtml`): day chips + the day in time order (`phTripDayRows`, `phTripTlrHtml`), the session
  opening in place, the folds stacked (CSS in the phone block).
- Today (`phTripTodayHtml`): the Next / Then card with the next venue's 中文 and its solid Driver card; the Driver card is per
  venue (`phTripDrvOn` = false · "1" the hotel · a venue id).
- Calendar (`phTripDayItems`, `phTripPopHtml`): program rows in their kind's colour over their part of the day; the card names
  the kind and venue + 中文; Plan opens that session (`data-ph-trip-open="id|plan|day|row"`, `phTripOpen(id, pane, day, ses)`).
- Session photos (`tses`, `phTripPics(..., ses)`); `PH_REN_BACKUP_FIELDS` now carries `trip`, `tday`, `tpart`, `tses`.
- The night before (`phTripNtfTick`, `phTripNtfSetHtml`, Settings · device "tripntf"): 8 pm trip-city time, page-run like the
  meal check-in; sw.js notificationclick passes `data.trip` on (`TRIP_OPEN` message, or `#trip=` in the address).
- New sprite icons: `i-walk`, `i-bus`, `i-train`, `i-nocam`, `i-coat`.

## Period pain: a range and several types; a made formula priced by its recipe (2026-10-31)
Her synth22 batch: "allow multiple select for pain type, including range for pain e.g. 4-6 etc" and "correspond formula refills
price to the inventory e.g. chai hu jia long go mu li tang". Her picks: How bad = **tap two numbers**; formula price = **its
recipe, always** (both the recommended options).
**Pain (the cycle day card, `phCycleSignPopHtml` q3):** tap 4 → 4; tap 6 → 4–6 (`painLo` 4, `painN` 6, cells 4 to 6 filled, none
pale under a range); a tap on a range → that one score; the same single score again or 0 → cleared. Pain type chips toggle
in and out: one type is stored as its word, two or more as a list in PH_CYCLE_FEELS order (old days read unchanged). New
helpers `phCycFeels(s)` and `phCycPainTxt(s)` (hoisted). Readers moved onto them: `phPatClues` (each type its own clue),
`phCycFbrSigns`, `phCycPeriodPain` (the top of a range is the worst day), `phCycUsual`, `phCycBoxSummary`, `phCycleSignLabel`,
the older popover's slider (it writes a single score and clears `painLo`) and its "Pain feels" row; `phCycleSelectChips`
takes a list as `cur` (a pick-several row). Painful? No keeps `painLo` in its Undo; `phCycleSignSet` drops a `painLo` that is
not below `painN`.
**Formula price:** her 27 Oct copy has CHAI HU JIA LONG GU MU LI TANG at $0.20/g with Mick active and a recipe (140 g, 11 herbs,
$26.88 = $0.192 → $0.20), so the numbers already agreed there; the price only ever moved at Make. Now `phRecipePricesSync`
squares every made-in-house jar with a recipe to `refRecipeCostPerG` after any save (1.2 s debounce, `phRecipePriceSoon` from
`savePharmacy` / `savePresc`) and after every pull, only while `__lcmSyncFresh` (vars + function declarations: savePharmacy
reaches it during boot). `phRecipeJarMap` picks the last-made recipe when several point at one jar. Inventory: Cost $/g and
Bottle $ show a "recipe" tag (Bottle $ = $/g × pack in the computed pill, not an edit button), hover "From its recipe: 140 g ·
11 herbs · $26.88 → $0.20/g". The To order page's Bottle $ (a supplier's price for buying) is unchanged.
**Found on the way (fixed):** the boot housekeeping's `setTimeout(…, 0)` read `window.__LCM_SYNC` before the parser had reached
the sync's `<script>` (measured: housekeeping done 3 s into a boot with no pull). Both it and the formula sync now start from
`phAfterScripts` (after DOMContentLoaded), so they wait for "lcm-sync-caught-up" as the 2026-08-22 rule meant.
**Tested** (sandbox, 1220 and 375): the tap sequence 4, 6, 5, 5, 6, 2, 2, 0, 3, 7 gave 4 · 4–6 · 5 · clear · 6 · 2–6 · 2 · clear ·
3 · 3–7 (word severe); types stabbing, cramping, back/leg in and out (word ↔ list ↔ none); No + Undo restores range and list;
clues counted each type (stabbing 2 days, cramping 2 days), periods' worst 6 and 7, Fang Bing Ren menstrual_pain_tend; a seeded
CHJLGMLT at $0.34 went to $0.20 on the catch-up, to $0.30 when Dang Shen went to $0.90, back to $0.20; housekeeping and the
formula sync wait until the catch-up (before: ran at 3 s); no console errors; no sideways scroll at 375.
**Not tested:** her signed-in data (the sandbox catalog's herb prices differ from hers), the Key2 at 360 × 469, Dispense's
patient price on a real dispense of a recipe-priced formula.

## 2026-11-01 — Messages: one "sent today" mark; the template groups fold
Idea 11 of her 2026-10-29 patient-profile audit, her words: "The Text / Messages / Copy tap leaves one mark, 'sent today', on
the patient, so the Due list and the band stop asking. The ten template groups fold to this plan's own set, the rest behind
'All ▾'." Measured on her 27 Oct export first: 670 patients, **3 messages ever prepared** (none sent, none planned), 65
follow-up records over 34 patients, **41 reviews overdue and never ticked, 9 check-ins due with 0 ticked**, 14 reviews ticked
done ever, 3 contact outcomes on patient records, 548 phones / 469 emails, 98 patients with an open plan: the text goes out
from the patient's Messages tab and the ✓ Done on Communications is a second trip she rarely makes. Mock
`messages-sent-mark-mock-2026-11-01.html` (pictures `ia/e11-*.png`; the "after" pictures are the real pages drawn by a
prototype through the harness); **her 9 picks, all the recommended option:** the mark = the Messages band's first tile; the
tap closes every due or overdue row of that patient; Undo in the one toast; Email leaves the mark too; this plan's own groups +
Herbs stay open; All = a chip under the groups (a row on the phone); All opens the other groups below as rows; the check-in
panel gets the same fold and the same mark, its row still closing on Done; no plan on file = the row's own kind + All.
**The mark** (`phMsgSentMark(name, row, via, f, keepRows)`, beside `phMsgMarkSent`): ONE entry on the patient's `contactLog`
(`{sent: sms | gmsg | copy | email, moment, label, kind, date, going: null, …}`, the shape the phase record and the
last-outcome reader already read), then every undone check-in / review of that patient due today or earlier (or the record the
composer is for) is done, an open acupuncture follow-up through `phAcuFuSetDone`, a gone-quiet row through
`phCommQuietDismiss`; it returns the undo (the mark out, every flag back, `acuFu` / `quietDismissedTouch` restored), null when
the save failed. `phMsgSentAfter` wraps it for both surfaces: the one toast ("✓ Copied · sent today · Review", "✓ Copied for
Google Messages · sent today · Review", "✓ Sent today · Review") with Undo, then `presBandsSync` so the band repaints in place
(the tile's sig is the mark's id). Patient tab (`presMsgClick`): Copy message marks after the copy lands (`phCkCopy`'s
after-copy fn, so a blocked copy leaves none), Messages marks as it opens, the Text / Email links mark as they go (the link
still opens: the handler returns false). Check-in panel (`phCkSentMark(via, prefix)`): the same four taps with `keepRows`, so
the open row stays on Due until her Done; `f.sent` gives "Sent · remind me tomorrow"; `phCkOpenMessages` routes through it (its
`phFlashShow` is gone, the toast carries Undo). Readers: `phPickLastGoing` skips marks (no outcome ever shadows the last real
one), the phase record's Check-ins line names a mark "sent · Review", its outcome cell skips them. `phMsgLastSent(key)` +
`phMsgSentWords` lead `PRES_BANDS.msg` with `{cls: "sent", ic: "check", v: Today | the date, t: "Sent · Review by Messages"}`.
**The fold** (`phMsgGroupsHtml`): shown = the groups `phCkGroupedMoments` already calls fitting (the active plan's track, a
second plan's track, Herbs for a herb row) + the group holding her pick; nothing fitting = the row's own kind (Herbs for a
herb row, Every visit for an acupuncture or gone-quiet one); the rest sit after one `.ph-mc-grp.all` row (`data-mc-all`,
`f.allOpen` on the form via `phMcFormDefaults`, `PH_MC_HOOKS`, `phMcClick`): "All · 7 ▾", a 32px / 6px chip in the label

## Flight lengths and "Sydney" time read home's own clock (2026-11-01)
**Her words:** "add my flights", then "yes fix it" (after I showed her MU792 SYD → NKG reading 7 h 50, which is 10 h 50).
**Found:** `phTripHomeTz` took the COMPUTER's clock as Sydney's. In Nanjing her laptop is set to China time (UTC+8), so the
out flight read 7 h 50 (10 h 50) and the flight home 14 h 05 (11 h 05); the trip's Today card read "10:47 am here · 10:47 am
Sydney". The routine pauses (`phMeTripWin`) compare clock times only and were not affected.
**Built:** `PH_TRIP_HOME_ZONE = "Australia/Sydney"` and `phTripZoneOff(ms)` (the zone's minutes ahead of UTC at that moment, from
`Intl.DateTimeFormat(...).formatToParts`; the computer's offset only if Intl throws). `phTripHomeTz(k)` asks it at 02:00 UTC of
day k (midday in Sydney, clear of both clock changes); the Today card's "Sydney" time is Sydney's wall clock (`homeD`).
**Tested** in the sandbox with the computer on China time: home offset 660 on 30 Oct / 15 Nov / 4 Oct / 1 Jan, 600 on 15 Jun /
5–6 Apr; her two flights 10 h 50 and 11 h 05 on the Travel page (`phTripTravHtml`, real render), a June trip 8 h 50; Today card
"10:47 am here · 1:47 pm Sydney" (Sydney's real time then: 13:47); no console errors. Picture: shots/flight-times-home-clock-fixed-2026-11-01.jpg.
**Not tested:** a computer on Sydney time (the code path is the same Intl read), the calendar flight card (it reads the same
`phTripFlightMin`), the Prescriptions search (the sandbox draws no list; checked on the live page after the push instead).
**Pages checked for the fact:** Travel (flights), the trip's Today card. Her data: flights entered 2026-11-01 from her Trip.com
emails (MU792 / MU791, seat 44A, PNR in `ref`), in her own Me row, not code.
**LIVE** 2026-11-01, build 20261101-141700 (publish afa6ae22 by the "B33 C4 LCM bugs" session on her "push live"; her "push live"
here the same minute). Checked on the live page in her Chrome: MU792 10 h 50, MU791 11 h 05, home offset 660; the
Prescriptions search narrows 41 → 1 → 0 → 41.

her 27 Oct export, read only: every page outside the patient file measured, before pictures, a report
(`app-usage-audit-2026-11-01.html`, artifact 8eovNZH3iHHs1KQbxq3ffi, the 19 `ia/au-before-*.png` inside it), two popup rounds.

**What the export said (Aug · Sep · Oct):** dispenses 25 · 33 · 34, appointments — · 118 · 115, To order arrivals 1 · 1 · 1:
daily. Formula refill batches 5 · 5 · 2 against 15–20 a month for five years (she still makes batches; the logging lagged, fixed
29 Oct). Stocktake fixes 182 · 49 · 18 (the counts are landing). Communications: Due in use, Compose 3 messages ever (Sep, 0
sent), Templates 92 seeds and none of hers, Prepared / Sent never used. Price review 0 sessions ever (moved into the Suppliers rows
29 Oct, her pick). Relocation set up, no date, 0 told. Guide 1 learned of 37 (built 21 Oct). Supplements reference: four
researched items as fixed text, read nowhere else. Dashboard, Stock statistics, Dispense history, Stock movements, Patient
directory, Intake review, End of day only read, so the export cannot tell; she opens them all (her answer).

**Her picks (rounds 1–2):** Communications = Due only, the other four behind one More ▾ chip; Formula refill, Stocktake,
Relocation, Guide, the read-only pages: keep as they are; Supplements reference folds into Settings › Patients › Supplements.
Mock `app-usage-mock-2026-11-01.html` (artifact 8Kknv1d7r79rJ2Khveu3hS, pictures `ia/au-mock-*.png` = the real app, a patched
copy through the `_ia-page.html` harness); eight mock picks, all the recommended ones: the More ▾ chip beside the strip with a
menu (not an inline unfold), menu lines with counts, the list as a table Kind · Usual dose · Shown, the researched text dropped
from the screens, Reference keeps its two lines, a patient's row pre-fills the usual dose (editable), Communications always opens
on Due, ✕ on her own kinds.

**Built:**
- `phCommSectionStripHtml` (next to `let phMsgSection`) draws the strip: Due, then the folded section that is open (if one is),
  then `<details class="ph-comm-more">` More ▾ with Compose · Templates n · Prepared n · Sent n (`PH_COMM_FOLDED`). The
  `[data-ph-msg-section]` click handler is unchanged; "Manage templates" in Compose and the Prepare landing still work, the
  picked section shows beside Due. CSS block after `.ph-msg-seg-opt.on`; on the phone the chip takes the strip's pill radius and
  the menu hangs from the right edge.

  dose; `phSuppKindDose` = a product's usual dose first, then that. `phSuppSettingsHtml`'s "The list" is now the table
  `.ph-supp-ktbl` (Kind · Usual dose · Shown · ✕ on her own kinds): `[data-supp-kind-dose]` saves on change like the product
  fields (same `change` listener), `[data-supp-kind-toggle]` as before, `[data-supp-kind-drop]` removes an own kind (the name
  `data-supp-kind-rm` already belongs to the patient's table). The dose-adjustment letter reads `phSuppKindDose` too.

  lines, `renderPhSupplementsPage` and its CSS. `PH_SUPPLEMENTS` stays (seed doses, the letter's words). Reference reads 2.

  640px }`, so the products table was 760px in a 657px card and its ✕ column sat past the edge. Both tables now use
  `#pharmacyPage .ph-vc-tbl.…` (two classes) and measure 655 in 657.

**Judgment calls:** a stale `activeTab = "supplements"` (a device that had the page open) renders the Inventory fallback, as

## 2026-11-01 · Calendar: hover no longer hides a block
**Her words:** "when i hover my mouse over an event the block disappears".
**Cause (measured on her live week 2–7 Nov, build 20261101-181400):** a block's layer is its place in the nest (`--z`, set by
`phApptCalBlockStyle` / `phC22JointLay`: the later block sits over the earlier one). Hover forced its own layer on top of that:
her events to 6 (`.ph-c22-life:hover`, left from the dashed design), visits to 20 (`.ph-appt-block:hover`). So hovering an
afternoon lecture (layer 3) lifted it over the Lunch and Herbs blocks drawn inside it (layer 5) and they vanished; 14 such
overlaps that week alone. Hovering a visit with one of her events inside it did the same, and an event at layer 7+ was pushed
down on hover.
**Fix (CSS only):** hover keeps the block's own layer: it brightens and rings, nothing else (her seamless pick 7, "hover
brightens, nothing grows", and pick D, "hover brightens only"). The open block (`.sel`) still rises, now 19 for her events too,
like a visit's, so an open one is never under a neighbour.
**Tested:** her live page in my own Chrome tab: before, hovering "Dr Zhang Xueguang 2:00" gave it layer 6 and the
spot under Lunch read the lecture; with the new rules (put into that tab only, then removed) the lecture stays at 3, brightens,
and Lunch and Herbs stay in view (shots/calendar-hover-before-2026-11-01.png, -after). The edited file in the sandbox: no hover
or focus rule on either block kind sets a layer (CSS rule walk), an opened event and an opened visit read 19.
**Not tested:** a real mouse hover on the edited file itself (the hidden sandbox pane did not take the hover); her phone (no
hover there).
**Pages checked for the fact:** Appointments grid (week and day), her events and visits; the chips above and below the day share
the rule (their hover never set a useful layer).
**LIVE** 2026-11-01, build 20261101-183100 (publish a88ca3d8, on her "push live"; it also carried two notes-only commits, 9fde75bb
and 01c24a59; the commit list matched the dry run). Checked on the live page: the build stamp, the visit hover rule with no layer,
the open event at 19, and the old `z-index: 20` hover rule gone.

## 2026-11-01 — Data check: batch makers, outgrown follow-ups, Twin jars, the missing-details ask

**Her ask:** after the app usage audit closed, her popup pick "LCM data check": every store in the 27 Oct export
(`backups/LCM-pharmacy-2026-10-27-before-update.json`, read only, loaded in the sandbox pane) read against the app's own rules.
Report `data-check-2026-11-01.html` (artifact NDVpFzLRcMqgRr2BWNyCmo; counts only, no patient names), mock
`data-check-mock-2026-11-01.html` (artifact 2eSThohB5gAgVkNA3S3v21; pictures `ia/dc-build-*.png` = the real app through the local
`_ia-page.html` harness). Both move to `mocks/` once live.

**What the export said (27 Oct):** 96 of this year's 107 batches and every one before 2026 (1,050) record no maker: only
`phBatchMade` wrote `source`, `refMakeCommit` wrote it only with a jar, `refMakeNoRecipeCommit` wrote null for a jar without a
supplier; Stock movements showed "—" and nothing else read it. 40 reviews and 9 check-ins overdue, 18 + 4 of them with a later
dispense to the same patient. Six Koda codes on two jars each (K585 Bai Zhu · Bai Zhu (Chao), K587, K621, K712, K876, K919), the
"(Chao)" twin mostly dormant, one stopped with 38 g on it. 86 active patients: 18 no sex, 27 no birth date, 7 no phone (the Cliniko
import writes only phone and email). Left as they are on her word: 30 phase-out jars with stock, 107 active jars never counted,
110 with no low-at, 1,731 unpriced pre-2026 dispenses, the two past Cliniko blocks ("Break", "Test Guy").

**Her picks (16 questions, every one the recommended option):** show the maker when missing and record it from now, no backfill;
a dispense closes that patient's older open reviews and check-ins, quietly (no folded line); Merge for twin jars with Undo, the
jar in use keeps its name, the item in Inventory's ⋯; Today's visit asks once for Sex · Birth date · Phone, whichever are missing,
one line in Worth a look; the maker of a batch into a jar = the jar's own source (Koda reads Koda); mock round: the label names
what is missing, keeper left in green, the done line without a new total, a lone Phone field at the right end of its line.

**Built:**
- `phRefillMaker(e, jar)` beside `phLogMovementInfo`: the entry's own source, else the jar's (by `targetId`, then by name), else
  `PH_IN_HOUSE_SUP`. Read by the refill branch of `phLogMovementInfo`, so Stock movements and its CSV (`phLogExportCsv`) carry it;
  Stock statistics still counts refills by kind. The three make paths (`phBatchMade`, `refMakeCommit`, `refMakeNoRecipeCommit`)
  always set `entry.source` now.
- `phFuContactRows`: a map of each patient's latest `dispensedAt` over `PHARMACY.followups`; a record older than that is skipped
  before its rows are built, so Due, the Dashboard strip, the nav badge and `phCommHiddenRows` agree. Nothing is written; the 22
  rows leave the moment the build opens on her records.
- Twin jars, before `// ---- the inventory grid ----`: `phTwinPairs` (every supplier row's code, grouped by supplier + code),
  `phTwinUse` (dispenses per jar: `deducted[].herbId`, the imported items by code or name), `phTwinKeeper` (not stopped, then
  stock on it, then the latest dispense, then the most), `phTwinPaint` / `phTwinOpen` / `phTwinClose` (the one `.ph-lk-sheet`
  shell, `.ph-merge-pair` rows from the duplicates finder), `phTwinMerge` (grams onto the keeper; low-at and note filled where the
  keeper has none; suppliers added; every `herbId` / `targetId` in the log, the stocktake records, the price reviews and an open
  count session re-pointed; the twin's name kept in `keep.aka`; the twin spliced out; one `herb-merge` log line; caches cleared;
  `phAfterQtyChange`) and `phTwinUndo` (every change replayed back, the twin at its old index, the log line out).
  `PH_TOPBAR_ACTIONS.inventory` is a function now: "Twin jars · n" shows only while a code sits on two jars. `findHerbByName`
  falls back to `h.aka`, so a prescription line or an old log item naming the twin still lands on the one jar (262 of the 264
  lines naming a twin carry a code anyway). The Log's "all" view leaves `herb-merge` out, like `patient-merge`.
- The ask: `phTodayAskHtml(rec)` (the Patient details hooks `data-pres-sex` / `data-pres-dob` / `data-pres-phone`, so the existing
  handlers write them: one door each), `phTodayAskWrap`, `phTodayAskRefresh` (the phone handler never repaints, so it calls this
  when the field sat in the line). `phTodayNudgesHtml` puts the row first, on a first visit too; `phTodayVisitHtml` and
  `presTpMainSections` (`todayAsk`) let Today's visit open on the line for a patient without sex and birth date instead of
  drawing nothing (the exam pages and the landing still wait for both; the profile's Start here card is unchanged). CSS after
  `.ph-today-nbtn.fill`: the fields 32 px, tinted, wrapping on a phone.

**Judgment calls:** the sheet finds seven pairs on her records, not six: K137 GUI ZHI FU LING WAN (Chi Shao) · (Bai Shao) under
Mick, two deliberate variants, the Chi Shao one stopped at 0 g; the rule would keep Bai Shao; told her, her row to leave. A merge
appends the twin's note to the keeper's when it differs. `h.aka` is shown nowhere. The maker is derived for display only: the
1,146 old entries keep no `source` (her pick, no backfill). The CLAUDE.md fold line from the app usage audit carried mojibake
